newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai September inflation rise below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Thai September inflation rise below expectations.

text.p: Thailand said on Tuesday that inflation in September rose 4.6 percent year-on-year, a level economic analysts said was lower than expected.

"I expected the September CPI (Consumer Price Index) would be lower than that of August. But I thought it would be around 5.2-5.3 percent against 5.5 last month and not this low," said Arporn Chewakrengkai, chief economist of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Inflation grew year-on-year by 5.5 percent in August.
Data released by the commerce ministry also showed that the September CPI rose 0.1 percent month-on-month compared with 1.0 percent in August.
Food prices went up only 0.1 percent from August while non-food prices rose 0.2 percent month-on-month.

Analysts said the inflation trend for the remainder of the year was expected to be down. This was because supplies of farm products were increasing in the market as harvesting progressed and seasonal floods disrupting the food chain were less severe this year than in 1995.
"I don't think food prices will be much of a problem this year," said Thanawat Patchimkul, a senior analyst at Seamico Research.
Analysts said they were now training their eyes on inflation data for October that would be announced by the commerce ministry on November 1.

A minimum wage increase of 12 baht to 157 baht per day ($6.28) in Bangkok and urban areas, higher oil prices and an approaching Thai election on November 17 could push inflation up more than expected from next month onwards, they added.
Thanawat said the minimum wage increase and higher oil prices compared with those last year would lead the way for cost-push inflation to set in.
The election campaign, traditionally accompanied by rampant vote buying using cash, was another inflationary factor, said an economist with a British brokerage who asked not to be named.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Arporn said the combined factors could push the November and December CPI up to 4.5-4.6 percent year-on-year from the 4.2-4.3 percent earlier anticipated.
For the whole of 1996, she forecast that inflation would average 5.7-5.8 percent compared with 5.5 percent projected by the Bank of Thailand.
